description: Searched in Slovak for an RSS/Atom feed for NBS aktuality and the supervision news stream ('nbs.sk RSS feed aktuality odber noviniek dohľad'). No RSS endpoint was found in search results. Evidence only of an on-site 'Prihlásenie na odber notifikácií' (notification subscription) control.

result.result_summary: No confirmed RSS/Atom URL for nbs.sk. An email/on-site notification subscription appears to exist but its mechanics were not established.

why_it_matters: Collection for the highest-velocity NBS channel will likely require HTML crawling and diffing rather than feed polling, which raises fragility and cost. A feed may still exist at an unadvertised path (e.g. /feed, /rss) and should be probed directly.

description: Searched in Slovak for a consolidated NBS sanctions register / list of imposed sanctions ('zoznam sankcií', 'rozhodnutia dohľadu'). Found the 'Metodická a sankčná činnosť' page and sector-specific 'Rozhodnutia' pages (e.g. under MiFID II/MiFIR), but no single cross-sector register of enforcement decisions against banks and payment institutions surfaced.

result.result_summary: Enforcement decisions appear to be scattered across sector pages and aktuality rather than centrally registered; no unified sanctions register URL identified.

why_it_matters: Enforcement is the sharpest signal of real supervisory priorities. Without a central register, the collector must stitch together several sector subtrees, and coverage completeness cannot be guaranteed.

description: Searched in Slovak for a consolidated NBS public-warning list on unauthorised business ('upozornenia', 'varovania', 'neoprávnené podnikanie'). Individual warnings were found as /aktuality/ items, and a third-party aggregator (banky.sk/varovania-nbs) surfaced, but a canonical NBS warning-list page on the current site was not identified.

result.result_summary: Warnings confirmed to exist and be published, but only as dispersed news items; canonical index page unlocated.

why_it_matters: Risks under-collection of grey-market signals and forces reliance on keyword filtering of the news stream, or on a non-authoritative third-party aggregator.

description: NBS states on its Vestník NBS page that the only binding wording of NBS legal regulations intended for the public is the version published in printed (listinná) form of the Vestník NBS; the website offers year-by-year archives (1993–2026) and an order address (vestnik@nbs.sk), functioning as a directory rather than full electronic publication.

result.result_summary: The legally authoritative text of some NBS acts is print-only by NBS's own declaration.

why_it_matters: Any automated collection of NBS opatrenia is by definition a non-binding copy. For acts also published in the Zbierka zákonov, SLOV-LEX provides an authoritative electronic substitute; for Vestník-only acts, a residual legal-certainty gap remains.

description: NBS's English legislation pages carry an explicit statement that only the original Slovak texts published in the Zbierka zákonov or the Vestník NBS have legal force, and that the most recent amendments may not yet have been translated into English.

result.result_summary: The English tree is an incomplete, lagging mirror by the regulator's own admission.

why_it_matters: Confirms that Slovak-language collection is mandatory for this cell and that any English-only pipeline would systematically miss the newest measures and deadlines.

description: The IS STATUS-DFT reporting system used by banks and payment institutions to submit výkazy to NBS requires administrator and user access-rights requests; only its surrounding documentation and electronic form definitions are public.

result.result_summary: Reporting content is behind authentication; only the reporting metadata layer (guidance, form catalogue, onboarding) is openly collectable.

why_it_matters: Actual reported data is out of reach; deadline intelligence must be derived from the mandating opatrenia and the public form catalogue instead.

description: Neither the NBS 'Konzultačné materiály' page nor the 'Materiály NBS v pripomienkovom konaní' page exposes an RSS/Atom feed or a consultation-specific subscription; only a general site-wide mailing list at https://nbs.sk/mailing-list/ was found.

result.result_summary: No machine-readable push channel for NBS consultations; polling or email parsing is required.

why_it_matters: Deadline monitoring must be built on scheduled scraping, which raises staleness and breakage risk for the highest-priority sources in this cell.

description: Direct slov-lex.sk legislative-process and comment URLs returned 'JavaScript required' via plain search/fetch. This is a rendering limitation, not evidence the pages are dead.

result.result_summary: Slov-Lex LP pages unverified by plain fetch; treated as live-but-JS-gated hypothesis.

why_it_matters: The single most authoritative consultation-deadline register in this cell needs headless-browser collection or a commercial API (LexAPI), which changes cost and architecture.

description: No dedicated, standing 'verejná konzultácia' hub page for financial-market topics was found on mfsr.sk; MF SR consultation activity appears episodically as press releases, programme pages (finančné inovácie/sandbox) and via slov-lex predbežná informácia / MPK.

result.result_summary: MF SR consultations are distributed across channels rather than centralised.

why_it_matters: A single-page monitor of MF SR would miss consultations; the collector must watch slov-lex, MF SR press releases and topic subtrees in parallel.

description: The NBS 'Konzultačné materiály' listing showed only three entries in total, two from 2015 and one from 2025 — a decade-long gap.

result.result_summary: NBS formal consultation-paper volume is very low; most real activity flows through MPK on slov-lex.

why_it_matters: Ranking sources by name alone would over-weight the consultation page; MPK/slov-lex is where the recurring signal actually is.

description: English-language searching surfaced far fewer live consultation artefacts than Slovak searching; NBS English pages mostly mirror already-issued decrees rather than open comment periods.

result.result_summary: English-only monitoring of this cell would miss most open comment periods and all MPK deadlines.

why_it_matters: Confirms local-language collection is mandatory, not optional, for the consultations/deadlines workstream in SK.

description: Repeated searches in English and Slovak for a global core-banking / digital-banking vendor case study naming a Slovak bank (Temenos, Finastra, Comarch, Backbase, Worldline, NCR, Diebold) returned no vendor customer-story page naming Tatra banka, Slovenska sporitelna, VUB or 365.bank.

result.result_summary: Only generic bank-profile and ranking pages surfaced; no vendor-hosted case study was located in this pass.

why_it_matters: Global vendors are the likeliest holders of large compliance-platform contracts at SK systemic banks; absence of findable case studies means their SK wins must be pursued via group-parent (Erste, Intesa, RBI) newsrooms and vendor press-release archives rather than country case studies.

description: No public announcement was found of an AML/KYC platform vendor selection by Tatra banka, Slovenska sporitelna or VUB in 2025-2026, in either Slovak or English.

result.result_summary: Searches returned regulatory background, bank profitability coverage and generic AML-vendor listicles, but no named bank-vendor AML/KYC deal.

why_it_matters: AML/KYC is a core compliance-spend category for this cell; if such deals are systematically unannounced, the cell must rely on onboarding/identity vendors (Softec, NFQES) and group-level announcements as proxies.

description: No private-bank RFP/tender publication channel was found for SK banks outside public procurement portals — no bank-hosted 'supplier portal', 'dodávatelia' or 'obstarávanie' page surfaced for the systemic private banks in this pass.

result.result_summary: Searches for supplier/tender pages on bank domains produced nothing; the assumption that SK private-bank buying is unpublished appears to hold.

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale: vendor-side publication is the only practical route, so collection weight should sit on vendor reference pages and press wires, not on buyer-side pages.

description: For payment-processing and card-scheme suppliers to SK banks (e.g. processors, ATM/POS estates, instant-payments infrastructure), no vendor page naming an SK bank was located; only journalistic coverage of the joint instant-payments programme.

result.result_summary: Instant-payments programme by Tatra banka, VUB and Slovenska sporitelna is documented in trade press, but the implementing vendor is not named in sources found.

why_it_matters: Payments infrastructure is deadline-driven (Instant Payments Regulation) and a major spend category; the implementing supplier remains unidentified and is a priority follow-up.

description: Searching TED in English for National Bank of Slovakia supervision-related notices returned only generic TED explainer pages and two unrelated notice PDFs, no confirmed NBS supervisory-IT notice.

result.result_summary: General TED documentation surfaced; no specific SK financial-supervision tender identified through the general web search layer.

why_it_matters: Confirms that general web search is the wrong instrument for this cell — TED's own Search API with buyer/CPV filters must be used rather than relying on indexed pages. Absence here is a search-method limitation, not evidence that such tenders do not exist.

description: No dedicated public procurement profile page was located for Slovenská záručná a rozvojová banka (SZRB), Fond ochrany vkladov or Garančný fond investícií within this run's searches; only a Wikipedia entry surfaced for SZRB.

result.result_summary: SZRB, FOV and GFI procurement pages not confirmed at a specific URL.

why_it_matters: These are exactly the state-linked financial bodies the cell targets. Their profiles almost certainly exist on ÚVO (profile search by name) but were not confirmed here, so no URL is asserted rather than inventing one.

description: UVOstat's API requires an ApiToken header; only /api/subjekty is free for registered users and other endpoints are paid, per its own documentation.

result.result_summary: Aggregator API is paywalled beyond one endpoint.

why_it_matters: Budget/dependency risk if the pipeline is designed around the aggregator; the free ÚVO/TED/CRZ primaries should remain the system of record.

description: No page fetch was attempted against uvo.gov.sk, ted.europa.eu, evo.isepvo.sk, josephine.proebiz.com, eks.sk, crz.gov.sk or metais during this run beyond the single NBS fetch; all other URLs come from search-result listings.

result.result_summary: URLs recorded from search indexes with stated confidence; liveness not asserted.

why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass must confirm reachability; several Slovak state portals have been restructured (uvo.gov.sk has both legacy '-4dd.html' and modern '/vyhladavanie/' URL forms), so redirects are expected rather than dead links.

description: No dedicated Slovakia-specific banking/payments regulatory alert feed was found for EY Slovensko in either language during this pass; EY did not appear in SK-language Big Four regulatory-news searches, unlike PwC, KPMG and Deloitte.

result.result_summary: PwC (danove-a-pravne-novinky), KPMG (danovky.sk) and Deloitte (cz-sk legal/consulting) all surfaced; EY did not.

why_it_matters: The Big Four are the highest-volume, most deadline-explicit interpreters of SK financial rules; a missing fourth channel is a real coverage hole, not evidence that none exists.

description: Havel & Partners, despite being a large CZ/SK firm, returned no SK banking/payments regulatory articles in the targeted query; the search engine explicitly returned no havelpartners hits.

result.result_summary: Query naming havelpartners returned only epravo/ULC/bpv/KPMG results.

why_it_matters: Havel is one of the largest firms operating in SK and almost certainly publishes; absence here is a search-coverage failure rather than a source absence.

description: No established Slovak-language shorthand was found for PSD3/PSR commentary — SK adviser content uses the English acronyms 'PSD2/PSD3', 'DORA', 'MiCA' untranslated, with only descriptive SK glosses (e.g. 'digitálna prevádzková odolnosť' for DORA).

result.result_summary: SK queries combining PSD3 with SK terms returned DORA/MiCA material and NBS pages, but no SK-language PSD3-specific adviser briefing.

why_it_matters: Collection queries must use the English acronyms even when searching SK-language sources; a purely SK-term query will miss most payments-regulation commentary.

description: Both PwC Slovensko and KPMG Slovensko route their timeliest regulatory content through email newsletters (dedicated subscription pages found for both). Newsletter-only items may never appear on the public web index.

result.result_summary: Subscription landing pages identified; no public archive of newsletter editions confirmed.

why_it_matters: Web crawling alone will lag or miss Big Four alerts; a subscribed mailbox is likely required for full coverage.

description: Several commercial vendor/blog pages purporting to explain SK KYC/AML and crypto rules (e.g. voveid.com blog, coredo.eu, lawzana.com listings) were encountered but are lead-generation content of unverified authorship, not adviser briefings.

result.result_summary: Encountered in en searches; deliberately not recorded as candidates.

why_it_matters: Including them would pollute the credibility distribution of this cell and risk propagating unsourced deadline claims.

description: No Slovakia-specific fintech/payments trade publication of the calibre of e.g. Czech or Polish fintech verticals surfaced in either sk or en searches; SK fintech coverage is scattered across general business media, crypto outlets and bank blogs.

result.result_summary: Searches on 'fintech Slovensko médiá' returned general portals (FinReport, Banky.sk), crypto media and corporate blogs, not a dedicated SK fintech trade title.

why_it_matters: Payments/fintech regulatory signal must be assembled from many low-volume outlets rather than one authoritative trade source, raising monitoring cost and miss risk.

description: Neither sk nor en searches surfaced Slovak media reporting of specific NBS enforcement actions or fines against banks/payment institutions.

result.result_summary: The en query on 'NBS enforcement fine' returned only NBS's own methodology/sanctions and warning-list pages, no journalistic enforcement coverage.

why_it_matters: Enforcement was a core rationale for this cell; if media do not systematically report sanctions, the enforcement picture must come from NBS sanction registers plus targeted per-entity searches instead.

description: Section paths for hnonline.sk (Finweb) and the trend.sk vs etrend.sk domain question were inferred from search snippets and outlet knowledge, not confirmed by a fetch in this pass.

result.result_summary: Search results named the outlets but did not return canonical section URLs.

why_it_matters: Crawler configuration for two major business outlets needs a URL-confirmation step before scheduling.

description: No confirmed EU regulatory newsletter with a recurring dedicated Slovakia section (beyond EPC country insights and EURACTIV.sk) was identified; Finextra/The Paypers did not appear in SK-specific results.

result.result_summary: En query naming Finextra and The Paypers returned no SK-tagged items from those outlets.

why_it_matters: SK is likely covered only episodically by pan-EU payments trade press; reliance should sit on national sources with EU trade press as opportunistic.

description: No SK-specific job-market analytics product was found that tracks compliance/regulatory hiring volumes over time (Profesia publishes general labour-market reports, but nothing scoped to banking regulation roles).

result.result_summary: Searches surfaced only raw listing pages and generic aggregators; the time-series signal must be constructed by the collector itself from repeated listing snapshots.

why_it_matters: Hiring-intensity as a leading indicator only works if snapshots are taken continuously; there is no back-fillable archive, so collection must start now.

description: No SK job posting explicitly naming DORA or PSD3 implementation at a named Slovak bank was retrieved in this pass.

result.result_summary: English-language search returned only advisory-firm marketing pages (PwC SK, CyberUpgrade, Validato) and a non-SK GRC job aggregator; the SK boards were not searchable at posting-text level from the search engine.

why_it_matters: Confirms that regulation acronyms in job ads are only reachable by querying the boards' own search (Profesia full-text), not via general web search — this constrains the collection design.

description: No dedicated, indexed archive of NBS supervisory officials' speeches other than the governor's page was located (e.g. no separate vice-governor or head-of-supervision speech archive).

result.result_summary: Vice-governor remarks were found only embedded in individual conference and news pages on nbs.sk.

why_it_matters: Supervisory-priority signals from non-governor officials must be harvested from the general Aktuality feed and event pages rather than a clean speech archive.

description: No SK 'compliance officer of the year' / regulatory-practitioner award or professional-body ranking was found; SK awards in scope are product- and bank-level (Zlatá minca, TREND Banka roka).

result.result_summary: Awards searches in Slovak returned only consumer-product and bank-of-the-year competitions.

why_it_matters: The awards channel gives actor-mapping value but little direct signal on regulatory implementation programmes; expectations for this sub-channel should be set low.

description: LinkedIn — the richest source for English-language senior regulatory-programme roles and for title changes signalling new functions — is login-walled and prohibits scraping.

result.result_summary: Only company landing pages were reachable without authentication.

why_it_matters: A whole class of the strongest weak signals is available only via manual analyst review or paid/official access; this is a standing cost, not a fixable bug.

description: No single consolidated, machine-readable NBS 'reporting submission calendar' page was located. Deadlines appear to be distributed across individual opatrenia (legal measures) as per-return tables (periodicity + deadline expressed as 'do 10. pracovného dňa', 'posledný kalendárny deň tretieho mesiaca', etc.) rather than as a published calendar file.

result.result_summary: sk queries for 'kalendár termínov predkladania výkazov' returned only the SDDS Plus advance PUBLICATION calendar and event calendars, not a submission calendar.

why_it_matters: Deadline extraction for this cell must be built by parsing legal-measure annex tables, not by scraping a calendar; collection design should budget for PDF table parsing.

description: I did not find an NBS-hosted page publishing national FINREP/COREP XBRL taxonomy packages or DPM artefacts; SK banks appear to consume EBA-published taxonomies directly, with NBS publishing only methodological reconciliation documents.

result.result_summary: sk+en queries combining NBS with FINREP/COREP/taxonómia surfaced EBA pages and NBS 'Metodické informácie' but no NBS taxonomy repository.

why_it_matters: Taxonomy-change tracking for SK banks should be anchored on EBA release cycles, with NBS pages watched only for national go-live/derogation notices.

description: The Štatistický zberový portál (ŠZP) and zber.statistics.sk submission areas require registered reporting-entity credentials; return catalogues and validation rule sets may live behind that login.

result.result_summary: Only public landing/registration pages were reachable in open search.

why_it_matters: Some of the densest deadline/taxonomy artefacts may be unreachable to open collection; plan to rely on the legal measures plus any public technical annexes instead.

description: Several NBS document URLs are opaque GUID-based download endpoints (nbs.sk/dokument/<uuid>/stiahnut) that were not fetched in this pass; their liveness is unverified here.

result.result_summary: URLs recorded from search result listings only.

why_it_matters: A deterministic liveness pass must resolve these before they are treated as stable anchors; GUID endpoints may rotate on site republish.

description: Searched specifically for an official Slov-Lex open API, ELI-based identifiers or a SPARQL endpoint for the Zbierka zákonov. No official, documented public API surfaced. What surfaced instead were a national standardisation study (MIRRI), a community scraper, and a commercial REST product (LexAPI/LexDATA).

result.result_summary: No confirmed official machine-readable API for Slov-Lex; ingestion will likely rely on the static.slov-lex.sk file mirror plus headless rendering of the eLegislatíva portal, or a commercial feed.

why_it_matters: Determines the engineering cost and fragility of the whole SK legislative-monitoring pipeline, and whether a paid feed is justified.

description: Searched in Slovak for open-data exports of NR SR parliamentary prints and voting records. The NR SR site exposes only HTML search/result pages; no official bulk export or documented API was found. The only structured route observed is the third-party Slovensko.Digital ecosystem.

result.result_summary: NR SR appears to offer no first-party open-data export for bills and votes; scraping the legacy ASP.NET pages is currently the default.

why_it_matters: The parliament stage is where final wording and effective dates are set; a fragile scraper here is a single point of failure for deadline tracking.

description: Searches in Slovak for 'Plán legislatívnych úloh vlády 2026' returned a large share of CZECH results (Ministerstvo financí ČR, vlada.gov.cz) because of the close similarity of Czech and Slovak legal vocabulary.

result.result_summary: Slovak-language queries about legislative planning are noisy with Czech-Republic sources; SK-specific results required the terms 'Slovenskej republiky' / 'SR' / site scoping.

why_it_matters: Any automated SK query layer must pin the country explicitly (site:*.gov.sk, 'Slovenskej republiky', 'Z. z.') or it will silently ingest Czech law as Slovak.

description: Multiple Slov-Lex legislative-process and comment URLs were reported by search as requiring JavaScript to display content. Not confirmed by a direct fetch in this pass — treated as a hypothesis, not a verdict, and certainly not as evidence the pages are dead.

result.result_summary: Slov-Lex eLegislatíva and pripomienky views are probably client-rendered; a plain HTTP fetch may return an empty shell.

why_it_matters: Drives the choice of collection method (headless browser or captured XHR endpoints) for the highest-value pointer source in this cell.

description: Attempted to locate a specific 'Predbežná informácia' (PI/2025/...) concerning the Payment Services Act 492/2009 Z. z. The PI register itself was found, but no matching payments-specific PI entry surfaced through search.

result.result_summary: PI register located and catalogued; the specific payments-related PI was not confirmed to exist.

why_it_matters: Absence in search is not absence in the register — the PI list must be enumerated directly rather than probed by keyword through a general search engine.

description: No URL in this slice was fetched and confirmed reachable by me; all were observed as search results. Several (rokovania.gov.sk/RVL/Material, nrsr.sk/dl/, lexapi.sk) are recorded on a single search-result sighting.

result.result_summary: All candidate URLs are supplied as unverified; liveness is left to the deterministic verification pass.

why_it_matters: Prevents downstream consumers from mistaking scout confidence for verified availability.

description: No official Slovak PSD3/PSR transposition tracker, draft bill, or announced national deadline was found in either language.

result.result_summary: SK-language searches on PSD3 transposition returned only law-firm commentary and an NBS explanatory PDF; no MF SR draft act, no Slov-Lex legislative process item, no NBS PSD3 hub. Consistent with PSD3/PSR not yet being in force, but means the SK transposition clock cannot be documented from a primary source today.

why_it_matters: PSD3/PSR is the largest pending payments obligation for SK banks and PSPs; the absence of a SK primary tracker means the run must rely on EU-level milestones until MF SR opens a comment procedure.

description: No published SBA (Slovenská banková asociácia) position paper on PSD3/PSR was located.

result.result_summary: SBA site returned general news items and one piece on an EU payment-security directive, but no PSD3 stanovisko. SBA's news archive may hold one behind non-indexed pages.

why_it_matters: Industry positions are the main indirect read on how SK banks expect to be affected; absence leaves a gap in sector-side signal for payments regulation.

description: No SK-specific ECB/SSM supervisory decision register was found — ECB does not publish individual supervisory decisions per bank.

result.result_summary: Searches surfaced only the aggregate list of supervised entities and general SSM materials. Slovakia currently has no domestically headquartered significant institution; nine SK LSIs are listed, two high-impact.

why_it_matters: Bank-level ECB decisions on SK entities are structurally non-public; the run must substitute the supervised-entities list, SREP aggregates and NBS LSI supervision outputs.

description: No stable Slovak-language term set exists for PSR (Payment Services Regulation) and AMLA.

result.result_summary: SK sources use the English acronyms PSD3/PSR/AMLA verbatim, or long descriptive phrases ('nariadenie o platobných službách'); no consolidated SK glossary was found beyond the NBS payments-law PDF.

why_it_matters: Local-language monitoring queries will under-recall unless English-in-Slovak acronyms are searched alongside descriptive SK phrases.

description: https://www.minv.gov.sk/?financna-policia returned getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND from this environment, while the equivalent www.minv.sk host fetched successfully.

result.result_summary: Treated as an environment/DNS resolution issue, NOT as a dead source. The gov.sk hostname appears in search results and is likely live; prefer www.minv.sk as the canonical collection host and let the deterministic verifier test both.

why_it_matters: Recording minv.gov.sk as dead would drop the single most important AML publisher in this cell.

description: minv.sk serves FSJ content via query-string URLs (?financna-policia=, ?povinnosti-a-sankcie-1) and the homepage fetch returned only top-level ministry navigation, so the full FSJ subpage map could not be enumerated from the landing page.

result.result_summary: Individual FSJ subpages and PDF paths were reachable only via search-engine discovery; no sitemap or document index was located.

why_it_matters: Collection must be built from a discovered URL seed list plus PDF-link harvesting, not from crawling the site tree; new usmernenia could otherwise be missed.

description: No dedicated public web page was found for NAKA / Národná kriminálna agentúra financial-crime investigative output, nor for a standalone SK sanctions-enforcement decision register, despite searching in Slovak.

result.result_summary: Sanctions competence is documented at MF SR (zák. 289/2016) and MZV SR, but no published register of national sanctions enforcement actions or asset-freeze statistics was located in this pass.

why_it_matters: Sanctions enforcement intensity — a key input for bank/PSP compliance demand — currently has no direct SK primary source in this cell.

description: No RSS/Atom feed, API, or structured 'aktuality' endpoint was identified for FSJ guidance or for the MF SR sanctions subtree.

result.result_summary: Only HTML pages and PDFs were observed; Slov-Lex is the one source in this cell with a plausible structured data channel (eZbierka).

why_it_matters: Timeliness of deadline detection will depend on polling frequency and HTML/PDF diffing rather than push notification.

description: No public, case-by-case decision database was found for the Slovak DPA (ÚOOÚ). A guessed path https://dataprotection.gov.sk/uoou/sk/content/rozhodnutia-uradu returned HTTP 404, and the site navigation exposes only 'Legislatíva a judikatúra', 'Metodiky a FAQ' and annual reports rather than a decision register.

result.result_summary: Individual ÚOOÚ decisions appear to reach the public mainly via annual reports, ad-hoc news items and third-party commentary (e.g. the mBank Art.13 case via soou.sk).

why_it_matters: GDPR enforcement against banks in SK cannot be tracked decision-by-decision from the authority itself; a proxy pipeline (annual reports + NGO/law-firm commentary + EDPB register) is required, and coverage will be lagged and incomplete.

description: The ÚOOÚ inspection-plan URL (/sk/urad/kontrola-spracuvania-osobnych-udajov/plan-kontrol-rok-2026/) was extracted from site navigation but not independently fetched in this pass; the per-year pattern is inferred, not confirmed.

result.result_summary: Recorded as a candidate with reduced confidence rather than as a verified live page.

why_it_matters: The verification pass should confirm the pattern before it is used as a scheduled annual collector.

description: No dedicated statutory financial ombudsman ('finančný ombudsman') institution was found for Slovakia. Searches in Slovak surfaced only the ADR framework under Act 391/2015 (Inštitút ARS SBA, SOI as residual body, consumer NGOs) plus the general Verejný ochranca práv, whose mandate covers public authorities rather than private banks.

result.result_summary: Ombudsman-type redress for SK banking is split between the SBA-run ARS institute, SOI and registered consumer NGOs; the general ombudsman is largely out of scope for bank conduct.

why_it_matters: Prevents mis-modelling the SK market against countries with a single financial ombudsman; complaint statistics are fragmented across several bodies, so no single complaint time-series exists.

description: SOI's competence over financial services is limited: financial-consumer protection sits with NBS, so SOI decisions touch retail finance only at the edges (leasing, ancillary credit offers, distance selling, general unfair-practice rules).

result.result_summary: SOI remains worth tracking but should be keyword-filtered rather than treated as a core banking-conduct feed.

why_it_matters: Avoids over-weighting SOI volume and mistaking general retail enforcement for banking-conduct signal.

description: No public, standalone NBS 'payment systems oversight report' (dohľad nad platobnými systémami) page was identified in this pass; oversight content appears embedded in NBS annual reports (výročná správa) chapters on platobný styk.

result.result_summary: Only older annual-report PDF chapters surfaced (vs2003/vs2004 kapitola Platobný styk); no current standalone oversight publication found.

why_it_matters: Oversight assessments of SIPS/card schemes are a key credibility anchor; if they exist only inside annual reports, collection must target report chapters, not a page.

description: Card scheme mandate calendars for Europe (Mastercard release bulletins, Visa Business News) are member-gated; only consolidated public rulebooks and third-party vendor digests are openly reachable.

result.result_summary: Public Visa rules PDF found; Mastercard bulletins require Mastercard Connect credentials.

why_it_matters: Scheme mandate deadlines are exactly the cell's stated blind spot; without member access the intelligence must be reconstructed from vendor commentary with lower confidence.

description: 'SIPS' is ambiguous: it denotes both the Slovak interbank system (Slovak Interbank Payment System / EURO SIPS) and the ECB Regulation on Systemically Important Payment Systems.

result.result_summary: A single SK query returned both NBS SIPS pages and an EUR-Lex SIPS Regulation summary.

why_it_matters: Automated collection keyed on 'SIPS' will produce false positives; queries must be disambiguated with 'platobný systém SIPS' + 'NBS'.

description: No established Slovak-language term was found for scheme-level artefacts such as 'scheme rulebook' or 'Routing and Verification Mechanism (RVM)'; SK material uses descriptive phrasing or the English terms.

result.result_summary: SK searches on scheme rulebooks returned EU/EN sources or generic 'pravidlá schémy' phrasing only.

why_it_matters: Scheme-rulebook monitoring for SK cannot rely on Slovak keywords; it must be done in English at EPC/scheme level and then mapped to SK participants.

description: No page was fetched in this pass; all URLs come from search-result metadata and are unverified for liveness. The Mastercard rules landing URL in particular is a well-known address that was not confirmed by a fetch.

result.result_summary: Search-only discovery; liveness left to the deterministic verification pass.

why_it_matters: Downstream verification should expect some redirects, especially on nbs.sk (site was restructured from www.nbs.sk/_img/... to nbs.sk/...) and nrsr.sk DocID links.

description: Search results referenced a codelist endpoint at https://subjekty.nbs.sk/api/cl and a 'Databáza na stiahnutie' bulk download on subjekty.nbs.sk, but I did not find published API documentation or terms of use for it during this pass.

result.result_summary: Bulk/API access to the NBS supervised-entity database is plausible but undocumented in what I could reach; treat the endpoint as a hypothesis to be confirmed by the deterministic verification pass.

why_it_matters: If a documented bulk export exists, the whole SK actor map can be maintained deterministically instead of by HTML scraping.

description: Beneficial-ownership entries recorded in the Obchodný register (since 2021) are legally non-public; only RPVS entries are publicly accessible, and RPVS covers only entities dealing with the public sector.

result.result_summary: There is no fully public, comprehensive UBO register for all SK financial entities.

why_it_matters: Ownership mapping of SK banks/PIs will be partial and must be assembled from RPVS + ORSR shareholder data + group disclosures, not from a single register.

description: The ECB list-of-supervised-entities URL captured is a date-stamped PDF (…202408…); the current edition will live at a different date-stamped path.

result.result_summary: URL recorded as-is; the stable entry point is the ECB Banking Supervision publications listing, which must be resolved at collection time.

why_it_matters: Hard-coding the date-stamped PDF will silently go stale or 404.

description: I did not locate a dedicated, separately published SK register page listing payment-service AGENTS as a standalone downloadable list (agenti platobných služieb); agents appear to sit inside the PSD2 register / subjekty.nbs.sk segments and the EBA central register.

result.result_summary: No standalone SK agents register found; use the EBA PSD2 central register agent records as the practical source.

why_it_matters: Agent networks are the distribution edge of the SK payments market; missing them would understate market reach.

description: ESMA registers (investment firms, trading venues, MiCA CASP register) and the Slovak trade-licence register (živnostenský register) were identified conceptually but not searched in depth within this cell's budget.

result.result_summary: Gap noted rather than filled.

why_it_matters: For sector=both, ESMA-side registers complete the supervised-actor perimeter.

description: SBA's website navigation (Úvod, Novinky, Členovia, Projekty a štandardy, O nás, Kontakt) contains no dedicated 'Stanoviská' / 'Pozičné dokumenty' / 'Publikácie' section, contrary to the seed-query assumption that a position-paper archive exists.

result.result_summary: Positions appear to be published as ordinary news items under /novinky/ with category tags; there is no separate, stable position-paper archive URL to anchor collection on.

why_it_matters: Collection design must scrape and classify the news stream rather than a clean position-paper index, and historical positions may be hard to retrieve; a Wayback-based backfill of /novinky/ should be planned.

description: No dedicated Slovak association of payment institutions / e-money institutions (a 'asociácia platobných inštitúcií' equivalent to EPIF or the EMA) was found in either Slovak or English searching.

result.result_summary: Searches on 'platobné inštitúcie združenie' returned leasing, securities-dealer and collection associations, but no payments-specific trade body. Non-bank payments interests appear to be carried by the Slovenská FinTech asociácia instead.

why_it_matters: For payments regulation specifically, there is no single dedicated national voice; the collection plan must rely on the fintech association, SBA, and EU-level bodies (EPC via SBA, EDFA) rather than a SK payments association that may not exist.

description: Two distinct-sounding fintech bodies surfaced: 'Slovenská FinTech asociácia' (slovakfintech.sk, est. 2018, IČO 51910497) and a 'Fintech & Insurtech Association of Slovakia' led by president Davy Čajko cited in the National FinTech Strategy coverage.

result.result_summary: It is unclear from the evidence gathered whether these are the same organisation under a rebranded name, or two competing bodies. No separate website for the latter was located.

why_it_matters: Attribution of fintech positions could be wrong, and one of the two bodies may be an uncollected source. Needs a targeted resolution step (ORSR/FinStat lookup on the president's name and on both trade names).

description: AOCP (Asociácia obchodníkov s cennými papiermi, the securities dealers' association) was confirmed to exist only indirectly, as a named partner association of SASS.

result.result_summary: No AOCP website, member list or position page was located in this pass; only third-party mentions.

why_it_matters: A capital-markets trade body relevant to MiFID/DORA/T+1 files is currently unaddressable. Needs a targeted follow-up search for its domain, or ORSR lookup.

description: Chambers of commerce with a plausible financial-sector policy role — SOPK (Slovenská obchodná a priemyselná komora) and AmCham Slovakia — produced no financial-regulation-specific hits despite both Slovak and English querying.

result.result_summary: Searches combining SOPK/AmCham with 'fintech', 'pracovná skupina', 'regulácia', 'zákon o bankách' returned no chamber position papers or working-group pages.

why_it_matters: Chambers may still run relevant committees; absence of evidence here is not evidence of absence, but they should not be scheduled for collection until a targeted site-level check is done.

description: The Slov-Lex legislative-process portal — the authoritative record of association comments in the inter-ministerial comment procedure — is JavaScript-rendered.

result.result_summary: Search-result metadata indicates the legislative-process and hromadné-pripomienky pages require JavaScript to display content; a plain HTTP fetch is expected to return an empty shell. Not tested directly in this pass, so this is a hypothesis, not a verdict.

why_it_matters: The single highest-value consultation source needs a headless-browser or API-based collector rather than simple HTTP scraping; budget for that in the collection architecture.

description: Three candidate URLs were constructed or inferred rather than observed: ruzsr.sk (RÚZ), blockchainslovakia.sk, and edfa.eu.

result.result_summary: Each organisation was confirmed to exist through independent evidence (HSR position PDF, Facebook page, SFA cooperation-agreement article), but their canonical domains were not returned by any search result.

why_it_matters: These must be resolved by the deterministic liveness/verification pass before being scheduled for collection; they are flagged with low confidence_score and access_status 'unverified'.

description: No Slovak-language disclosure or T&C-change page was found for UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia, a.s., pobočka zahraničnej banky (SK branch). Searches returned only registry/aggregator and directory entries, no unicreditbank.sk disclosure hub.

result.result_summary: Branch exists (IČO 47251336, Šancová 1/A Bratislava) but its own regulatory-disclosure surface was not located in this pass; as an EU-passported branch its Pillar 3 sits at Czech parent level.

why_it_matters: A materially sized corporate/retail player in SK would be missing from the cell's disclosure coverage; its Pillar 3 must be sourced from the Czech parent instead.

description: Fetch of the SLSP 'Finančné ukazovatele' hub returned prose but no link list — document links appear to be injected client-side or served from cdn0.erstegroup.com.

result.result_summary: Hub reachable, but a plain HTTP fetch does not expose the PDF inventory.

why_it_matters: Collection for SLSP will need a rendering crawler or CDN path enumeration rather than simple HTML link extraction.

description: No RSS/Atom feed or structured API for T&C-change notices was identified at SLSP, VÚB, Tatra banka, ČSOB or 365.bank.

result.result_summary: All change notices are HTML pages or dated PDFs; no push mechanism found.

why_it_matters: Deadline tracking must rely on scheduled diffing, so cadence and change-detection design matter more than for feed-based sources.

description: The full text of Opatrenie NBS 16/2014 was found on the legacy nbs.sk path (/_img/documents/...); NBS has since migrated to a new site structure.

result.result_summary: URL recorded as-is; not verified reachable. A 404 here would mean 'moved', not 'withdrawn'.

why_it_matters: The measure is the schema for all bank disclosures in this cell; the canonical current URL should be re-resolved on the new nbs.sk.
